chapter_title: The Mathematics of Maybe: Introduction to Probability

concepts.title: Experimental Probability
concepts.definition: Roll, toss, count what actually happens: the share of trials that produced the outcome is its observed chance.
concepts.key_idea: Built from real tallies, not from ideal assumptions.
question_patterns: In 50 tosses of a die, a 4 appeared 8 times; calculate its observed chance.
From the tally, what share of the days was rainy?
Compute the observed share of heads in 200 coin tosses that gave 92 heads.
Find the relative frequency of a defect if 3 of 80 items failed inspection.
Estimate the chance of a missed bus from one month's record of 6 misses in 44 school days.

solution_steps.explain: The observed share is successful outcomes over attempts made.

solution_steps.action: Simplify the fraction to its lowest terms or convert to a decimal
solution_steps.explain: Reducing the fraction makes the probability easier to interpret and compare.

solution_steps.action: Verify the result lies between 0 and 1
solution_steps.explain: Any valid probability must fall in the range 0 to 1, confirming the count was correct.

concepts.title: Theoretical Probability
concepts.definition: Assume every face has the same chance and reason it out on paper: wanted results over all attainable results.
concepts.key_idea: Counts from a fair setup; no trial runs needed.
question_patterns: One card is drawn from a full deck of 52 cards; what is the likelihood that it is a king?
Find the probability of drawing a heart from a full deck of 52 cards.
Calculate the chance of two heads in two fair tosses.
What share of a full deck is hearts? Give the probability.
State the chance of an even number on one fair die.

solution_steps.explain: Wanted outcomes divided by every equally likely outcome.

solution_steps.action: Simplify the fraction or convert to a decimal
solution_steps.explain: Reducing the fraction makes the probability easier to interpret and compare.

solution_steps.action: Confirm the result is between 0 and 1
solution_steps.explain: A valid probability always lies in the range 0 to 1, which checks the counts were correct.

concepts.title: Sample Space
concepts.definition: Every distinct result a chance setup can produce, written as a single full list.
concepts.key_idea: One line per outcome; nothing twice, nothing missing.
question_patterns: List the sample space for one fair coin toss.
Write down all outcomes for rolling one die.
What is the total outcome count when two coins are tossed together?
Determine the sample size for a letter drawn from the word Maths.
Enumerate the outcomes of a spinner landing on 1 through 5.

solution_steps.explain: Identify every distinct result the setup could produce.
The size of the list is the sample size.

solution_steps.action: Check that every entry is distinct and the list is complete
solution_steps.explain: No outcome should appear twice and no possible outcome should be missing, ensuring a valid sample space.
